sources.title: Hydroponic Ganja seizure at Chennai International Airport

sources.excerpt: The Government has decided that the existing 15 days’ stockholding limit for bulk consumers is relaxed to 30 days, subject to the condition that the quantity of stock held beyond the existing 15 days’ limit, shall be sourced exclusively from sugar imported under Advance Authorisation Scheme (AAS) and Tariff Rate Quota (TRQ). The stockholding limit for purchase from the open market shall remain unchanged and will be restricted to 15 days’ consumption only. The government has also put in place a mechanism for the declaration and weekly disclosure of sugar stocks every Friday by bulk consumers through the Department of Food and Public Distribution's online portal @ https://foodstock.dfpd.gov.in/

sources.excerpt: Strengthening Adaptive Development and Humane Aptitude for National Advancement ( Sādhana ) Shrinkhala 2026 is being organised by the Capacity Building Commission (CBC) as a nationwide series of regional consultative workshops. The series is dedicated to the transformation of Training Institutes under Mission Karmayogi as capacity building institutions . Sādhana Saptah 2026, observed from 2 to 8 April 2026, was one of the largest collaborative capacity building initiatives in the country. Carrying forward the spirit of consultation, the Shrinkhala seeks to extend the national dialogue on institutional reform to the States and their Training Institutes. The first workshop in the series will be held at Vijayawada, Andhra Pradesh, on 29th and 30th September 2026.

sources.author: Ministry of Communications
sources.title: TRAI Assesses Mobile Network Quality Across Chennai City under TN LSA, during the month of July 2026
sources.excerpt: The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has released findings of Independent Drive Test (IDT) conducted across Chennai City under TN LSA, during the month of July 2026, for information of general telecom consumers. The purpose of this drive test is to assess and verify real time quality of mobile network services (both voice & data) provided by Telecom Service Providers (TSPs). During the IDT, TRAI captures performance of TSPs for key Quality of Service (QoS) parameters like Coverage, Call Drop Rate (CDR), Call Setup Success Rate (CSSR), data Download (DL) and Upload (UL) throughput etc., which are then published to inform Consumers and encourage TSPs to improve their services.

The conference, he emphasised, must translate into concrete action and measurable outcomes. “The Centre and the states are one agriculture team. He stressed that commitments made by states at the conference must be fulfilled. Otherwise, the entire exercise would lose its purpose.

sources.title: SEMICON India 2026 Concludes Successfully, Showcasing India’s Growing Role in the Global Semiconductor Ecosystem
sources.excerpt: SEMICON India 2026, the fifth edition of India’s flagship semiconductor conference, concluded successfully today at Yashobhoomi, New Delhi, marking another step in the development of India’s semiconductor ecosystem. Held from 17–19 September 2026 under the theme “Silicon to Systems: Building the Ecosystem,” the event featured over 600 exhibitors, including around 300 international participants, representatives from 52 countries, and over 150 speakers. Six Country Pavilions representing Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, the Netherlands, Singapore and Sweden, along with 12 State Pavilions, a Startup Pavilion, Workforce Development Zone, Innovation Showcase & Student Hackathon, showcased different dimensions of the semiconductor value chain. The event recorded 51,656 total registrations and cumulative footfall of about 40,000.

sources.title: TRAI Assesses Mobile Network Quality Across Chennai City under TN LSA, during the month of July 2026
sources.excerpt: The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has released findings of Independent Drive Test (IDT) conducted across Chennai City under TN LSA, during the month of July 2026, for information of general telecom consumers. The purpose of this drive test is to assess and verify real time quality of mobile network services (both voice & data) provided by Telecom Service Providers (TSPs). During the IDT, TRAI captures performance of TSPs for key Quality of Service (QoS) parameters like Coverage, Call Drop Rate (CDR), Call Setup Success Rate (CSSR), data Download (DL) and Upload (UL) throughput etc., which are then published to inform Consumers and encourage TSPs to improve their services.

sources.title: SEMICON India 2026 Concludes Successfully, Showcasing India’s Growing Role in the Global Semiconductor Ecosystem
sources.excerpt: SEMICON India 2026, the fifth edition of India’s flagship semiconductor conference, concluded successfully today at Yashobhoomi, New Delhi, marking another step in the development of India’s semiconductor ecosystem. Held from 17–19 September 2026 under the theme “Silicon to Systems: Building the Ecosystem,” the event featured over 600 exhibitors, including around 300 international participants, representatives from 52 countries, and over 150 speakers. Six Country Pavilions representing Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, the Netherlands, Singapore and Sweden, along with 12 State Pavilions, a Startup Pavilion, Workforce Development Zone, Innovation Showcase & Student Hackathon, showcased different dimensions of the semiconductor value chain. The event recorded 51,656 total registrations and cumulative footfall of about 40,000.

The series is dedicated to the transformation of Training Institutes under Mission Karmayogi as capacity building institutions . Sādhana Saptah 2026, observed from 2 to 8 April 2026, was one of the largest collaborative capacity building initiatives in the country. sources.title: Ranga Belia Tagore's Cooperative Promotes Women’s Livelihoods through Traditional Crafts
sources.excerpt: Tagore Cooperative in Ranga Belia in the Sundarbans has emerged as a centre for hand-batik, handloom and tailoring activities, providing livelihood opportunities to women in the region. The products are largely handmade and reflect traditional craft practices adapted to the local context. The cooperative has been working since 1976 with the objective of promoting women’s economic self-reliance in the Sundarbans, where employment opportunities outside agriculture and traditional livelihoods remain limited. According to the cooperative, around 30,000 women have received various forms of training over the years. At present, more than 100 women are engaged with the cooperative, including several long-serving members.

sources.title: TRAI Assesses Mobile Network Quality on Gandhidham to Santhalpur National Highway (NH-27) in Gujarat LSA
sources.excerpt: The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has released findings of Independent Drive Test (IDT) conducted on Gandhidham to Santhalpur National Highway (NH-27) in Gujarat LSA , during the month of July 2026, for information of general telecom consumers. The purpose of this drive test is to assess and verify real time quality of mobile network services (both voice & data) provided by Telecom Service Providers (TSPs). During the IDT, TRAI captures performance of TSPs for key Quality of Service (QoS) parameters like Coverage, Call Drop Rate (CDR), Call Setup Success Rate (CSSR), data Download (DL) and Upload (UL) throughput etc., which are then published to inform Consumers and encourage TSPs to improve their services.

sources.title: PIB Hyderabad Organises First-Ever Press Tour to Kolkata

sources.title: Kolkata Metro: From India’s First Metro to a Multi-Corridor Urban Transport Network
sources.excerpt: Kolkata Metro, India's first Metro railway system, has evolved from its modest beginning of a 3.4-km stretch between Esplanade and Bhowanipore (now Netaji Bhavan) in 1984 into a multi-corridor urban rapid transit network. The Metro project in Kolkata commenced in 1972, while India's first Metro commercial service began on October 24, 1984, covering 3.4 km and three intermediate stations. As of 2025, the network had expanded to five colour-coded lines, 58 stations and 73.42 km of route length.

sources.title: India International Water Week 2026
sources.excerpt: Water does not follow a single path. A drop of rain can seep into the soil, fill a pond, recharge a well, or flow into a river. How we capture, conserve, and manage that water can shape lives and livelihoods. Across India, communities have traditionally built structures to capture rain, recharge groundwater, and restore rivers and traditional water bodies. Today, as the demand for water grows all around us, it has become even more important to revive community participation for ensuring water security, along with scientific planning, strong institutions and sustained action.

sources.author: Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
sources.title: Kolkata Metro: From India’s First Metro to a Multi-Corridor Urban Transport Network
sources.excerpt: Kolkata Metro, India's first Metro railway system, has evolved from its modest beginning of a 3.4-km stretch between Esplanade and Bhowanipore (now Netaji Bhavan) in 1984 into a multi-corridor urban rapid transit network. The Metro project in Kolkata commenced in 1972, while India's first Metro commercial service began on October 24, 1984, covering 3.4 km and three intermediate stations. As of 2025, the network had expanded to five colour-coded lines, 58 stations and 73.42 km of route length.

sources.author: Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
sources.title: Kolkata Metro: From India’s First Metro to a Multi-Corridor Urban Transport Network
sources.excerpt: Kolkata Metro, India's first Metro railway system, has evolved from its modest beginning of a 3.4-km stretch between Esplanade and Bhowanipore (now Netaji Bhavan) in 1984 into a multi-corridor urban rapid transit network. The Metro project in Kolkata commenced in 1972, while India's first Metro commercial service began on October 24, 1984, covering 3.4 km and three intermediate stations. As of 2025, the network had expanded to five colour-coded lines, 58 stations and 73.42 km of route length.

sources.title: Kolkata Metro: From India’s First Metro to a Multi-Corridor Urban Transport Network
sources.excerpt: Kolkata Metro, India's first Metro railway system, has evolved from its modest beginning of a 3.4-km stretch between Esplanade and Bhowanipore (now Netaji Bhavan) in 1984 into a multi-corridor urban rapid transit network. The Metro project in Kolkata commenced in 1972, while India's first Metro commercial service began on October 24, 1984, covering 3.4 km and three intermediate stations. As of 2025, the network had expanded to five colour-coded lines, 58 stations and 73.42 km of route length.

sources.title: Power from Waste
sources.excerpt: Across India, organic waste is finding a second life as fuel, electricity and valuable manure. Under the Swachh Bharat Mission, launched in October 2014 , scientific management of municipal solid waste has remained a core objective. As the Mission evolved, organic waste has been recognised as a valuable resource to produce clean energy. Biogas, produced through the anaerobic decomposition of organic waste, is among the most viable, economical and environmentally friendly cooking fuels available. The by-product slurry is rich in nitrogen and serves as an effective organic fertilizer. It reduces dependence on chemical inputs, lowers costs and helps maintain soil fertility. This delivers a dual benefit from a single initiative.

sources.title: Kolkata Metro: From India’s First Metro to a Multi-Corridor Urban Transport Network
sources.excerpt: Kolkata Metro, India's first Metro railway system, has evolved from its modest beginning of a 3.4-km stretch between Esplanade and Bhowanipore (now Netaji Bhavan) in 1984 into a multi-corridor urban rapid transit network. The Metro project in Kolkata commenced in 1972, while India's first Metro commercial service began on October 24, 1984, covering 3.4 km and three intermediate stations. As of 2025, the network had expanded to five colour-coded lines, 58 stations and 73.42 km of route length.

sources.title: Prime Minister shares Sanskrit Subhashitam highlighting the importance of dedication to one’s duties
sources.excerpt: The Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi has shared a Sanskrit Subhashitam highlighting that those who remain devoted to their respective duties attain the highest perfection. He emphasised that those who diligently and sincerely perform their duties should understand how dedicated action can lead to the highest state of fulfilment. The Prime Minister shared a Sanskrit Subhashitam- “स्वे स्वे कर्मण्यभिरतः संसिद्धिं लभते नरः। स्वकर्मनिरतः सिद्धिं यथा विन्दति तच्छृणु॥” The Subhashitam conveys that those who remain devoted to their respective duties attain the highest perfection. Therefore, those who diligently perform their duties should learn how the highest state of perfection can be attained through dedicated and sincere action.

sources.title: Ayush Emerges as One of India’s Fastest-Growing Service Sectors, RIS Study Estimates US$36.92 Billion Economy
sources.excerpt: The Ayush services sector has emerged as one of India’s fastest-growing service sectors, with its economic contribution estimated at US$36.92 billion in FY2024-25, according to a new study by the Research and Information System for Developing Countries (RIS). Registering a 16.91 per cent CAGR since FY2022-23, the sector is increasingly contributing to India’s economic growth through healthcare, wellness, employment generation and Medical Value Travel. The study projects that the Ayush services economy could scale to US$216–318 billion by 2047, underlining its significant potential to contribute to the Viksit Bharat @2047 vision. The Report was formally released during the 11th Ayurveda Day celebrations in Nagpur on 23rd September.

sources.excerpt: The Ayush services sector has emerged as one of India’s fastest-growing service sectors, with its economic contribution estimated at US$36.92 billion in FY2024-25, according to a new study by the Research and Information System for Developing Countries (RIS). Registering a 16.91 per cent CAGR since FY2022-23, the sector is increasingly contributing to India’s economic growth through healthcare, wellness, employment generation and Medical Value Travel. The study projects that the Ayush services economy could scale to US$216–318 billion by 2047, underlining its significant potential to contribute to the Viksit Bharat @2047 vision. The study projects that the Ayush services economy could scale to US$216–318 billion by 2047, underlining its significant potential to contribute to the Viksit Bharat @2047 vision. sources.title: Incentive Scheme for Promotion of Domestic PNG Connections
sources.excerpt: Piped Natural Gas (PNG) expansion is an important part of India’s transition towards cleaner household energy and energy security. Supplying PNG to homes is part of City Gas Distribution (CGD) network development. Such a network comprises pipelines and allied facilities that serve households, commercial establishments, and industrial units. Entities authorised by the Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB) develop it. PNGRB has authorised entities in 309 Geographical Areas (GAs) . Together, these areas span the entire mainland of the country. As of 18 August 2026, there were 1.74 crore domestic PNG connections across the country.

sources.excerpt: Coal mining remains central to India’s energy security and industrial growth. CIL has driven a strategic shift towards modernising both underground (UG) and open-cast (OC) operations for greater efficiency, safety and sustainability. Advanced digital interventions – IoT, AI and data analytics – are reducing hazard exposure, improving recovery rates and enabling predictive maintenance, smart control rooms, automated dispatch and ‘Smart Mines’.

sources.excerpt: The 43rd edition of Indian Coast Guard (ICG) Commanders’ Conference commenced in New Delhi from September 17, 2026. On the opening day of the three-day conference, Raksha Rajya Mantri Shri Sanjay Seth interacted with DG ICG Director General Paramesh Sivamani and Coast Guard Commanders on pivotal issues concerning national and maritime security. In his address, Raksha Rajya Mantri commended ICG for safeguarding maritime interests by ensuring coastal security and being the first responder in times of distress at sea, saving precious lives irrespective of the nationality. He called upon ICG to remain prepared for emerging maritime security challenges by keeping pace with rapid technological advancements.

sources.excerpt: India’s agricultural carbon market has moved from policy to the farm level, with more than 2,500 smallholder farmers in Punjab and Haryana set to receive digital payments for adopting regenerative farming practices. The first payments were released at a programme organised at Punjab Agricultural University (PAU), Ludhiana, marking a new link between sustainable agricultural practices and additional income for farmers. Dr M. L. Jat, Secretary, Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE) and Director General, ICAR, initiated the Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) to 2,550 farmers from Punjab and Haryana.

sources.excerpt: The Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (DAHD), Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Government of India, in collaboration with the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH), organised a three-day PVS–PPP Targeted Support Workshop on “FMD-Free Zone Development in India” from 15–17 September 2026 at the National Agricultural Science Complex (NASC), New Delhi. The workshop brought together representatives from the DAHD, 12 State Animal Husbandry Departments, experts from WOAH, Paris, CDDL/RDDLs, NDDB, ICAR Research Institutions, industry, livestock value-chain stakeholders and technical experts to strengthen the pathway towards establishing FMD-free zones and compartments in India.

sources.title: Capacity Building Commission (CBC) to start Regional Workshops (Sadhana Shrinkhala) to Transform Training Institutes under Mission Karmayogi
sources.excerpt: Strengthening Adaptive Development and Humane Aptitude for National Advancement ( Sādhana ) Shrinkhala 2026 is being organised by the Capacity Building Commission (CBC) as a nationwide series of regional consultative workshops. The series is dedicated to the transformation of Training Institutes under Mission Karmayogi as capacity building institutions . Sādhana Saptah 2026, observed from 2 to 8 April 2026, was one of the largest collaborative capacity building initiatives in the country. Carrying forward the spirit of consultation, the Shrinkhala seeks to extend the national dialogue on institutional reform to the States and their Training Institutes. sources.title: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Calls for Time-Bound Action on State Commitments at Southern Regional Agriculture Conference
sources.excerpt: Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, while addressing the concluding session of the Regional Agriculture Conference for Southern States in Hyderabad, directed states to complete their agricultural targets and commitments within the stipulated timelines. He said states must act seriously on the actionable points identified during the day-long deliberations. The conference, he emphasised, must translate into concrete action and measurable outcomes. “The Centre and the states are one agriculture team. Our scientists, our farmers, officers of the Central and state governments, all together form one agriculture team. We must work together,” Shri Chouhan said. He stressed that commitments made by states at the conference must be fulfilled. Otherwise, the entire exercise would lose its purpose.

sources.title: SEMICON India 2026 Concludes Successfully, Showcasing India’s Growing Role in the Global Semiconductor Ecosystem
sources.excerpt: SEMICON India 2026, the fifth edition of India’s flagship semiconductor conference, concluded successfully today at Yashobhoomi, New Delhi, marking another step in the development of India’s semiconductor ecosystem. Held from 17–19 September 2026 under the theme “Silicon to Systems: Building the Ecosystem,” the event featured over 600 exhibitors, including around 300 international participants, representatives from 52 countries, and over 150 speakers. Six Country Pavilions representing Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, the Netherlands, Singapore and Sweden, along with 12 State Pavilions, a Startup Pavilion, Workforce Development Zone, Innovation Showcase & Student Hackathon, showcased different dimensions of the semiconductor value chain. The event recorded 51,656 total registrations and cumulative footfall of about 40,000.

sources.author: Ministry of Earth Sciences
sources.title: Pilot Phase of NIRMaL Sāgar launched in Visakhapatnam
sources.excerpt: Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS), Ministry of Earth Sciences, Govt. of India, Hyderabad, in association with the Andhra University and Vignana Bharati (VIBHA) has launched the pilot phase of the NIRMaL sāgar programme (National Initiative for Remediation of Marine Litter), a clean ocean initiative to establish the first integrated marine litter tracking framework in Visakhapatnam on 19th September 2026 (Saturday), the concluding day of the week-long Swachh Sagar Surakshit Sagar 5.0 campaign in an assembly arranged in Andhra University Auditorium in RK Beach. The pilot program was inaugurated by the Dr. T. Srinivasa Kumar, Secretary, Ministry of Earth Sciences in the presence of Shri. M. Shribharat Hon’ble Member of Parliament, Visakhapatanam and several other dignitaries.

sources.excerpt: The Centre for Trade and Investment Law (CTIL), Indian Institute of Foreign Trade, organised a webinar on “WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies: Legal Framework and Policy Prospects” on 21 September 2026. The webinar coincided with the commencement of WTO Fish Week and followed India’s ratification of the WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies (AFS) on 20 July 2026. International trade law experts, fisheries specialists and policymakers participated in discussions on implementation of the Agreement, one year after its entry into force, as well as ongoing negotiations on additional disciplines concerning overcapacity and overfishing.

sources.title: Kolkata Metro: From India’s First Metro to a Multi-Corridor Urban Transport Network
sources.excerpt: Kolkata Metro, India's first Metro railway system, has evolved from its modest beginning of a 3.4-km stretch between Esplanade and Bhowanipore (now Netaji Bhavan) in 1984 into a multi-corridor urban rapid transit network. The Metro project in Kolkata commenced in 1972, while India's first Metro commercial service began on October 24, 1984, covering 3.4 km and three intermediate stations. As of 2025, the network had expanded to five colour-coded lines, 58 stations and 73.42 km of route length.

sources.author: PIB Backgrounder
sources.title: Power from Waste
sources.excerpt: Across India, organic waste is finding a second life as fuel, electricity and valuable manure. Under the Swachh Bharat Mission, launched in October 2014 , scientific management of municipal solid waste has remained a core objective. As the Mission evolved, organic waste has been recognised as a valuable resource to produce clean energy. Biogas, produced through the anaerobic decomposition of organic waste, is among the most viable, economical and environmentally friendly cooking fuels available. The by-product slurry is rich in nitrogen and serves as an effective organic fertilizer. It reduces dependence on chemical inputs, lowers costs and helps maintain soil fertility. This delivers a dual benefit from a single initiative.
